column2: 中古英语 occasioun ← 中古法语 occasion ← 古法语 occasiun ← 拉丁语 occāsiō（时机），由 ob-（向下）＋ cadere（落下）构成
column3: a particular time when a certain event happens
column5: We met again on a formal occasion last spring.|The occasion called for a short speech.
column6: a moment that falls into place – 恰好落到眼前的那个时点
column7: 场合：按约定时间聚起来的那一场|时机：机会正好落下来的那一刻

column2: 中古英语 occasyonal ← 中世纪拉丁语 occāsiōnālis 与古法语 ocasionel，由 occasion ＋ -al 构成
column3: happening from time to time but not regularly
column5: She pays occasional visits to her old school.|We had occasional showers throughout the afternoon.
column6: happening only at scattered moments – 只在零星几个时点发生
column7: 偶尔的：时点稀疏地散落着，不成规律|临时的：只在个别场合才派上用场

column2: 中古英语 occupacioun ← 中古法语 occupacion ← 拉丁语 occupātiō，源自 occupāre（占据），由 ob-（向）＋ capere（拿）构成
column3: the work someone does regularly, or the holding of a place by force
column5: Please state your name and occupation below.|The occupation of the city lasted four years.
column6: what fills a person time or a space – 把时间或空间占满的东西
column7: 职业：日常把时间占满的那件事|占领：把一处地方占住不放|占用：占着某个空间或时段

column2: 中古英语 occupien ← 古法语 occuper ← 拉丁语 occupāre（取得、占据），由 ob-（向）＋ capere（拿）构成
column3: to fill a space or a period of time, or to take control of a place
column5: Boxes occupy most of the small room.|The children occupied themselves with a puzzle.
column6: to take and hold a space – 拿住并占着一处不放
column7: 占据：把空间实实地占满|使忙碌：把某人的时间占满

column2: 古英语 of／æf（从、离开）← 原始西日耳曼语 *ab ← 原始日耳曼语 *ab，与 of 同源后分化
column3: away from a place, or no longer working or connected
column5: He drove off before we could wave.|Please switch the lights off when leaving.
column6: away from or detached from something – 从某物上移开、断开
column7: 离开：从原处移开|关闭：电路断开不再接通|不工作：不在运转状态

column2: 中古英语 office ← 古法语 office ← 拉丁语 officium（职责、职位），由 opus（工作）＋ facere（做）缩合而成
column3: a room or building where people do administrative work
column5: She works in a small office downtown.|He held office for almost ten years.
column6: a place or post carrying assigned duties – 承担职责的处所或位置
column7: 办公室：处理事务的那间屋子|职务：所承担的那份职责

column2: 中古英语 officer ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 officer ← 晚期拉丁语 officiarius，源自 officium（职务）
column3: a person holding a position of authority in an organization
column5: A police officer checked our travel documents.|The officer gave orders to his unit.
column6: a person who holds an official post – 担着公职的人
column7: 官员：在机构里担公职的人|军官：军中担指挥职的人

column2: 中古英语 official ← 古法语 official ← 拉丁语 officiālis，源自 officium（职责）
column3: coming from an authority, or a person holding public office
column5: The official report was published last week.|A senior official answered questions from reporters.
column6: backed by or belonging to authority – 由权力机构认可或所属的
column7: 官方的：经权力机构认可发布的|官员：机构里担公职的人

column2: 古英语 ofspring（后代），由 of（自）＋ spring（涌出）构成
column3: the young produced by a person or animal
column5: The pair raised three offspring that summer.|Many animals protect their offspring fiercely.
column6: what springs off from a parent – 从亲代分出来的下一代
column7: 后代：从亲代分出的下一代|子女：人所生的后代

column2: 古英语 ānlīċ／ǣnlīċ（唯一的）← 原始日耳曼语 *ainalīkaz，由 one ＋ -ly 构成
column3: no more than this, or with nothing else besides
column5: She was the only person still waiting.|It costs only a few pounds now.
column6: standing alone with nothing beside – 旁边没有别的，只此一个
column7: 仅仅：数量或程度上不超过这个|唯一的：同类里只剩这一个

column2: 借自意大利语 opera ← 拉丁语 opera（工作、作品），是 opus 的复数形式
column3: a play in which the story is mostly sung
column5: They watched an Italian opera last night.|The opera runs for nearly four hours.
column6: a staged work carried by singing – 靠歌唱撑起来的舞台作品

column2: 由 opportune ＋ -ity 构成 ← 中古法语 opportunité ← 拉丁语 opportūnitās（合时宜）
column3: a set of conditions that makes something possible
column5: This job offers a real opportunity to learn.|He missed the opportunity to speak up.
column6: a favourable opening that appears – 出现在眼前的有利缺口

column2: 由 optic ＋ -al 构成；optic 一支 ← 中世纪拉丁语 opticus ← 希腊语 optikos（与看有关的）
column3: relating to sight or to the behaviour of light
column5: The optical illusion fooled almost everyone here.|Optical fibres carry signals over long distances.
column6: to do with seeing and with light – 与看和光有关的
column7: 视觉的：与眼睛所见有关|光学的：与光的性质及器件有关

column2: 由 optimist ＋ -ic 构成；optimist ← 法语 optimiste，由拉丁语 optimum（最好的）造出
column3: expecting good things to happen
column5: She stayed optimistic despite the bad news.|Forecasters remain optimistic about the coming harvest.
column6: expecting the better outcome – 倾向于认定会有好结果

column2: 借自新拉丁语，为拉丁语 optimus（最好的）的中性形式
column3: the most favourable point or condition for something
column5: The plants grow best at optimum temperature.|Engineers searched for the optimum between cost and speed.
column6: the best available point in a range – 一段范围里最好的那一点
column7: 最佳的：在可选范围里最好的|最佳状态：正处在那个最好点上的情形

column2: 借自拉丁语 orchēstra（古希腊剧场中歌队表演的场地）
column3: a large group of musicians playing together
column5: The orchestra tuned up before the concert.|She plays cello in the city orchestra.
column6: a large body of instrumentalists – 一大群合奏的器乐手

column2: 古英语 ōþer（其他的、第二个）← 原始日耳曼语 *anþeraz ← 原始印欧语 *h₂énteros
column3: different from the one already mentioned
column5: The other students had already gone home.|Try the other door on your left.
column6: not this one but a different one – 不是这个，是别的那个
column7: 其他的：除此之外的那些|另一个：两者之中不是这个的那个

column2: 由 our ＋ selves 构成
column3: used to refer back to the speakers as a group
column5: We finished the whole job by ourselves.|We should not blame ourselves for this.
column6: the speakers referring back to themselves – 说话人一方指回自身

column2: 古英语 ūt（向外）与 ūte（在外）← 原始日耳曼语 *ūt／*ūtai ← 原始印欧语 *úd（向上、离开）
column3: away from the inside of a place
column5: She walked out without saying a word.|The children are out in the garden.
column6: moving or being beyond an enclosure – 从围合处出去或处在其外
column7: 向外：从里往外移动|在外：位置处在围合之外

column2: 早期 out-fit 的变体，来自动词短语 fit out（装配齐备）
column3: a set of clothes worn together, or to supply with equipment
column5: She wore a bright outfit to the party.|They outfitted the boat for a long voyage.
column6: a complete set fitted out for use – 配齐了备用的一整套
column7: 装备：为某用途配齐的一套器具|全套服装：成套穿在身上的衣物

column2: 由 out ＋ -ing 构成；古英语有同义的 yting（外出、行程）
column3: a short trip taken for pleasure
column5: The class went on an outing to the coast.|Rain spoiled our Sunday outing completely.
column6: a brief trip out and back – 出去一趟就回的短程行程

column2: 中古英语 outlete，源自 outleten（放出），由 out- ＋ let 构成
column3: an opening that lets something out, or a shop selling one maker goods
column5: Water escaped through a narrow outlet below.|The factory outlet sells shoes at lower prices.
column6: a point where something is let out – 让东西放出去的那个口
column7: 出口：让水、气、电放出去的口|专卖店：厂家把货直接放出去的店

column2: 由 out ＋ line 复合而成
column3: the line marking the outer edge of something, or a short general account
column5: He drew the outline of a mountain.|She outlined her plan in a few minutes.
column6: the outer line with the inside left empty – 只有外框、内部未填的那条线
column7: 轮廓：物体外缘那条线|概述：只给框架不填细节的说明

column2: 由 out- ＋ look 复合而成
column3: the way someone views things, or how something is likely to develop
column5: His outlook on life changed after the trip.|The outlook for small farms remains uncertain.
column6: what one sees looking outward – 向外看出去所见的景象
column7: 观点：向外看事情所取的角度|前景：往前看到的可能情形

column2: 由 out ＋ put 复合而成，是动词短语 put out 的名词化
column3: the amount something produces, or to produce and send out
column5: The factory doubled its output last year.|The program outputs a short summary file.
column6: what is put out from a process – 从一道过程里送出来的东西
column7: 产出：一段时间里生产出的量|输出：把结果送出去这个动作

column2: 中古英语 outrage ← 古法语 outrage／oultrage（过分）← 俗拉丁语 *ultrāticum ← 拉丁语 ultrā（超出）；后被重新理解为 out- ＋ rage，读音随之改变，但两者本无词源关系
column3: great anger at something felt to be very wrong
column5: The decision caused outrage among local residents.|His remarks outraged almost everyone present.
column6: anger at something that goes too far – 对越过界限之事的强烈愤怒
column7: 愤怒：因不公之事而起的强烈怒气|激怒：使人生出这种怒气

column2: 由 out ＋ set 构成，取代了更早的 outsetting
column3: the very beginning of something
column5: He knew the risks from the outset.|State your aim clearly at the outset.
column6: the point of setting out – 动身出发的那一点

column2: 由 out ＋ side 复合而成
column3: beyond the limits of a place, or the outer part of something
column5: The children played outside until it grew dark.|We painted the outside of the shed.
column6: the region beyond a boundary – 界线之外的那一片
column7: 在外面：位置落在界线以外|外部：物体朝外的那一面

column2: 源自 outstand，由 out ＋ standing 构成
column3: clearly better than others, or still not settled
column5: She gave an outstanding performance that evening.|Two invoices are still outstanding this month.
column6: standing out from the level around it – 从周围齐平处凸出来
column7: 杰出的：明显高出同侧水平|未解决的：仍悬在外没有了结

column2: 古英语 ofer ← 原始西日耳曼语 *obar ← 原始日耳曼语 *uber ← 原始印欧语 *upér（在上、越过）
column3: above or across something, or brought to an end
column5: A bird flew over the quiet lake.|The meeting was over by four today.
column6: above and across to the far side – 在上方并越到另一侧
column7: 在上方：位置高于某物|结束：越过终点、不再继续
